title: WH Ford RTC Fueling System Repairs
description: ***This solicitation is a Small Business set-a-sided, restricted to 100% small business only.***The project includes repairs and upgrades to an existing fuel storage and dispensing facility. Work includes repairing concrete and pavement; removing water from an underground communications access box; installing an emergency fuel shutoff station and leak detection equipment; and repairing and recoating fuel system canopies, piping, and related components. Additional work includes replacing tank vents, repairing and improving grounding systems, modifying platforms to provide safe access to tank equipment, and upgrading the automatic tank gauging (ATG) system and associated controls.

Please acknowledge receipt of this Amendment 01 below & return it in your File #1 Contract Documentation. _________________________________________________________________________________________________ The Air Force Services Center (AFSVC), headquartered at Joint Base San Antonio- Lackland, Texas, delivers Services programs and activities to build and sustain ready and resilient Airmen, Guardians and families. Air Force Services Center supports the bases, major commands and air staff by providing technical assistance, new initiatives, developing programs and procedures and managing central support functions. Air Force Services Center ensures successful operation of essential food, fitness, childcare, lodging and recreation opportunities for military members and their families. The Center�s responsibilities include preparing responses to high-level inquiries, providing technical assistance to the field and developing new programs that support major command and installation activities. The Financial Management Directorate (VF) manages the Nonappropriated Fund Public Accountant Contract Audit program centrally which supports a worldwide mission providing an oversight of internal controls, cash management and financial information to installations at the enterprise level. Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations provide support services and activities for military personnel, families and authorized patrons. Proper management and accountability of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) resources are critical to ensuring continued service delivery and the protection of government interests. Regular audits are required to evaluate the financial status, internal controls, and operational effectiveness of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) operations. The Air Force Services Center Financial Management, Strategic Policy & Financial Operations, AFSVC/VFSF manages and administers audit oversight to Central Funds and the Public Accountant Contract Audit (PACA) Program to ensure compliance with annual audit requirements of financial statements audits of the NAFIs and that adequate audit coverage is provided Air Force wide for the Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) Services activities. The Contractor shall conduct comprehensive audits of the financial statements, transactions, internal controls, and performance of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations and activities. AFSVC is seeking to contract an audit firm for a 5-year period, structured with a Base Year and four (4) subsequent Option Years. AFSVC intends to issue initial Base Year task orders requiring dual-year financial statement audits encompassing two distinct historical fiscal years as designated in the individual task orders (e.g., FY24 and FY25). While financial statement audits will examine specific, historical fiscal years, performance audits will be conducted on an as-needed basis determined by an annual risk assessment, with the specific scope defined in individual task orders. Only written responses from responsible sources will be considered. Any prospective contractor must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to be eligible for award. description: Purpose: The Army Contracting Command - Rock Island (ACC-RI) at Picatinny, Picatinny Arsenal, NJ 07806-5000 is conducting a Market Survey on behalf of the Project Manager Howitzer Systems (PM-HS). Experience: A description of the respondent�s manufacturing experience of the 155-mm Cannon Tubes, or similar products, within the last five (5) years to include past performance. Include applicable description of experience with each cannon tube. 3. Production Process: A description of the respondent�s existing 155-mm cannon production process to include all major manufacturing stages and the operations/equipment utilized for each, as well as all supporting subcontractors. The description must detail the entire production lifecycle, including, but not limited to: 3.1. A detailed description of the respondents bore and outside diameter cold working capabilities to include autofrettage. 3.2. A detailed description of the respondent�s boring and milling capabilities along with the capacity or each (length, weight, outer/inner diameters). 3.3. A detailed description of the respondent's rifling capabilities, including methods (e.g., swage, broach, or single-point machining) and general experience with standard 155-mm rifling configurations (lands, grooves, and twist rates). 3.4. A detailed description of the respondent or subcontractor coating capabilities for chrome bore coatings on a steel tube up to 30 ft long and up to 7,500 pounds in weight. Provide the maximum length and weight of tube that can be coated by respondent. 3.5. A detailed description of the respondent�s protective coating and painting capabilities. 3.6. Detailed description of the respondent�s advanced manufacturing capabilities and growth areas. 4. Production Capacity: A description of the respondent�s current maximum monthly capacity to produce 155-mm cannon tubes. Please specify separate production rate capacity for each and if different manufacturing lines, tooling, or subcontractors are utilized. 5. Production Availability: A description of the respondent�s maximum caliber capability and projected available capacity to produce 155-mm cannon tubes within 18 months from the date of these sources sought. 6. Optimization opportunity: A description of the domestic facilities, equipment, machines and tooling required to increase the available capacity to produce 155-mm cannon tubes up to ten (10) tubes per month, regardless of caliber, within 36 months from the date of this source sought. Specify whether the projected production capacity for each tube type is dedicated or shared across multiple lines. Provide an NTE ROM cost estimate for an initial production quantity of forty (40) cannon tubes (broken down by caliber or indicating pricing for a combined/flexible mix). 7. Material: A detailed description of the respondent�s cannon tube source material grade, respondent(s) and processing. Please acknowledge receipt of this Amendment 01 below & return it in your File #1 Contract Documentation. _________________________________________________________________________________________________ The Air Force Services Center (AFSVC), headquartered at Joint Base San Antonio- Lackland, Texas, delivers Services programs and activities to build and sustain ready and resilient Airmen, Guardians and families. Air Force Services Center supports the bases, major commands and air staff by providing technical assistance, new initiatives, developing programs and procedures and managing central support functions. Air Force Services Center ensures successful operation of essential food, fitness, childcare, lodging and recreation opportunities for military members and their families. The Center�s responsibilities include preparing responses to high-level inquiries, providing technical assistance to the field and developing new programs that support major command and installation activities. The Financial Management Directorate (VF) manages the Nonappropriated Fund Public Accountant Contract Audit program centrally which supports a worldwide mission providing an oversight of internal controls, cash management and financial information to installations at the enterprise level. Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations provide support services and activities for military personnel, families and authorized patrons. Proper management and accountability of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) resources are critical to ensuring continued service delivery and the protection of government interests. Regular audits are required to evaluate the financial status, internal controls, and operational effectiveness of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) operations. The Air Force Services Center Financial Management, Strategic Policy & Financial Operations, AFSVC/VFSF manages and administers audit oversight to Central Funds and the Public Accountant Contract Audit (PACA) Program to ensure compliance with annual audit requirements of financial statements audits of the NAFIs and that adequate audit coverage is provided Air Force wide for the Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) Services activities. The Contractor shall conduct comprehensive audits of the financial statements, transactions, internal controls, and performance of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations and activities. AFSVC is seeking to contract an audit firm for a 5-year period, structured with a Base Year and four (4) subsequent Option Years. AFSVC intends to issue initial Base Year task orders requiring dual-year financial statement audits encompassing two distinct historical fiscal years as designated in the individual task orders (e.g., FY24 and FY25). While financial statement audits will examine specific, historical fiscal years, performance audits will be conducted on an as-needed basis determined by an annual risk assessment, with the specific scope defined in individual task orders. Submit all quotes no later than (NLT) 2:00PM, CST, Tuesdsy, 23 Nov 2026 via email to valerie.baltimore@us.af.mil and whitney.ward.1@us.af.mil. The RFQ closes at 2:00PM, CST, Tuesday, 23 Nov 2026.

title: Chief Joseph Dam Main Unit XJ Breaker Disconnects Modernization
description: EVENT DETAILS: Date: 3 December 2026 Time: 0930-1430 PT Format: Presentation & Site walk Registration Due Date: 23 November 2026, 1200 PT; Please register by returning completed Request for Visit Authority (RVA) by email to: Sarah Malowicki, Project Manager, at sarah.m.malowicki@usace.army.mil, AND Londres Medranda, Contract Specialist, at londres.medranda@usace.army.mil. Confirmation email will be sent upon receipt of completed RVA. Who Should Attend: Interested vendors, including small businesses, large businesses, and other industry partners. Attendance is limited to 2 personnel per company. Attendance is limited to United States Citizens. Attendance at this event is not mandatory. Pre-registration is required. DESCRIPTION: In accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(a) Early exchanges with industry, the United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District (NWS) is hosting an Industry Day on 3 December 2026 at Chief Joseph Dam in Bridgeport, Washington. This Industry Day provides an opportunity for interested parties to inspect the existing 15.5KV Main Unit XJ Breaker disconnects first-hand. By hosting this first-hand inspection, the government aims to gather technical feedback and explore industry alternatives for modernizing this equipment. We are seeking input from qualified, experienced sources, capable of performing this modernization work. PROJECT BACKGROUND: At Chief Joseph Dam the current Unit 1-16 XJ Breaker disconnects are original BBC (Brown Boveri Corporation) equipment and rated 6000A according to the BBC shop drawings. The switch operators are pneumatically driven, and are actuated by operation of a complex key interlocking scheme with the circuit breaker. The load side and source side disconnects are mechanically linked and simultaneously operated by a single shared pneumatic actuating system. The current Units 17-27 breaker disconnects are original GE equipment. The load side and source side disconnects are mechanically linked and simultaneously controlled by mechanically operated hand crank. USACE is evaluating options to improve reliability, maintainability, remote-operating capability, and overall generating-unit availability. � Option 1: Refurbish and restore existing disconnect switches to an approved condition equivalent to original design intent, as technically feasible. Integrate motorized mechanisms on the switch arms to enable remote operation, and comprehensively overhaul and test the existing main unit breakers to ensure optimal system protection. � Option 2: Replace the disconnect switches with new electrically operated units and refurbish the existing breakers. � Option 3: Replace both the disconnect switches (with new electrically operated units) and the main unit circuit breakers. � Option 4: Replace the entire switchgear assembly with new enclosures, modern electrically operated disconnect switches, and new circuit breakers (includes associated controls, protection, buswork and new enclosure). Chief Joseph Dam has several critical limitations that affect this project, primarily related to space constraints. This Industry day will present the options under consideration, obtain industry feedback on technical feasibility and constructability, and identify potential risks, constraints and cost drivers. USACE is requesting feedback on the following questions and relevant, non-binding information: Does your company have the ability, capacity, interest and willingness to perform the proposed options? Does your company have experience with comparable medium-voltage/high-current generation-station disconnect and breaker modernization projects? We are not currently requiring quotes or bids, however rough estimates would be greatly appreciated. Recommended technical approaches or alternatives Major schedule outage, access, safety, supply-chain or constructability risks. Do you believe all aspects of this requirement could be successfully performed by the small business sector under NAICS 237990 (Size standard $45M)? (Yes/No). If No, what estimated percentage do you think can be subcontracted out to small business? The U.S. Government is not obligated to pay for any information, documentation, demonstrations, or data provided, nor will it reimburse any costs incurred by your organization in preparing responses, traveling to, or participating in this Industry Day and physical equipment inspection. All costs associated with attending this event and participating in this information exchange are solely at the responding party�s expense. title: B--ShakeAlert Production System Code Review
description: THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ). This presolicitation notice is for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation, request for quotation, or commitment by the Government to award a purchase order. The Department of the Interior (DOI), United States Geological Survey (USGS) Acquisition Team, seeks a qualified firm to perform an independent code review of the ShakeAlert Earthquake Early Warning (EEW) Production System. ShakeAlert is a mission-critical system that operates continuously to detect earthquakes and provide life-safety warnings to more than 50 million people along the U.S. West Coast. The production environment comprises numerous real-time, safety-critical software components that have evolved over many years and are maintained by a small team under significant operational constraints. The objective of this work is to improve the reliability, maintainability, and long-term sustainability of the ShakeAlert production code base through two complementary activities: - A rigorous, module-by-module review of source code quality, correctness, and maintainability. - An assessment of current software development and deployment practices, with concrete recommendations for modernizing the GitLab CI/CD pipeline and workflow. Work will be performed in phases over a period not to exceed 12 months. All work shall be conducted with regular coordination with USGS ShakeAlert staff. All work can be performed remotely. ACQUISITION PROCEDURES This acquisition will be conducted using simplified procedures for commercial products and commercial services pursuant to the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO), Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12. The Government intends to award a firm fixed-price purchase order to the vendor whose quotation represents the best value to the Government. Quotations will be evaluated by the following trade-off factors: Technical Approach, Relevant Experience, Personnel Qualifications, Past Performance and Price. Non-priced factors will be evaluated using confidence ratings as specified in the solicitation. Anticipated Award Date is January 4, 2027. Pursuant to RFO 12.201-1(c)(2), the Government intends to solicit quotations directly from a minimum of three qualified sources. Pursuant to RFO 5.201(b)(2), this presolicitation notice is being posted to the Government Point of Entry (GPE) in lieu of posting the solicitation. The RFQ will be issued to the sources selected for solicitation. Requests for the RFQ from other eligible small business concerns will be addressed in accordance with RFO 5.202. Responsible sources may submit a response that will be considered by the Government and shall include the following: - Company name; - System for Award Management (SAM) Unique Entity Identifier (UEI); - Business size and socioeconomic status, if applicable; - Point of contact, telephone number, and email address; and - Capability statement demonstrating the firm's ability and qualifications to perform the work. All responsible sources responding to this notice will be considered by the Government to determine the sources to be solicited. Point of Contact: Charlan Fejarang, Contracting Officer Email: charlan_fejarang@ios.doi.gov

title: Industry Day: Chief Joseph Dam Main Unit XJ Breaker Disconnects Modernization
description: EVENT DETAILS: Date: 3 December 2026 Time: 0930-1430 PT Format: Presentation & Site walk Registration Due Date: 23 November 2026, 1200 PT; Please register by returning completed Request for Visit Authority (RVA) by email to: Sarah Malowicki, Project Manager, at sarah.m.malowicki@usace.army.mil, AND Londres Medranda, Contract Specialist, at londres.medranda@usace.army.mil. Confirmation email will be sent upon receipt of completed RVA. Who Should Attend: Interested vendors, including small businesses, large businesses, and other industry partners. Attendance is limited to 2 personnel per company. Attendance is limited to United States Citizens. Attendance at this event is not mandatory. Pre-registration is required. DESCRIPTION: In accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(a) Early exchanges with industry, the United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District (NWS) is hosting an Industry Day on 3 December 2026 at Chief Joseph Dam in Bridgeport, Washington. This Industry Day provides an opportunity for interested parties to inspect the existing 15.5KV Main Unit XJ Breaker disconnects first-hand. By hosting this first-hand inspection, the government aims to gather technical feedback and explore industry alternatives for modernizing this equipment. We are seeking input from qualified, experienced sources, capable of performing this modernization work. PROJECT BACKGROUND: At Chief Joseph Dam the current Unit 1-16 XJ Breaker disconnects are original BBC (Brown Boveri Corporation) equipment and rated 6000A according to the BBC shop drawings. The switch operators are pneumatically driven, and are actuated by operation of a complex key interlocking scheme with the circuit breaker. The load side and source side disconnects are mechanically linked and simultaneously operated by a single shared pneumatic actuating system. The current Units 17-27 breaker disconnects are original GE equipment. The load side and source side disconnects are mechanically linked and simultaneously controlled by mechanically operated hand crank. USACE is evaluating options to improve reliability, maintainability, remote-operating capability, and overall generating-unit availability. � Option 1: Refurbish and restore existing disconnect switches to an approved condition equivalent to original design intent, as technically feasible. Integrate motorized mechanisms on the switch arms to enable remote operation, and comprehensively overhaul and test the existing main unit breakers to ensure optimal system protection. � Option 2: Replace the disconnect switches with new electrically operated units and refurbish the existing breakers. � Option 3: Replace both the disconnect switches (with new electrically operated units) and the main unit circuit breakers. � Option 4: Replace the entire switchgear assembly with new enclosures, modern electrically operated disconnect switches, and new circuit breakers (includes associated controls, protection, buswork and new enclosure). Chief Joseph Dam has several critical limitations that affect this project, primarily related to space constraints. This Industry day will present the options under consideration, obtain industry feedback on technical feasibility and constructability, and identify potential risks, constraints and cost drivers. USACE is requesting feedback on the following questions and relevant, non-binding information: Does your company have the ability, capacity, interest and willingness to perform the proposed options? Does your company have experience with comparable medium-voltage/high-current generation-station disconnect and breaker modernization projects? We are not currently requiring quotes or bids, however rough estimates would be greatly appreciated. Recommended technical approaches or alternatives Major schedule outage, access, safety, supply-chain or constructability risks. Do you believe all aspects of this requirement could be successfully performed by the small business sector under NAICS 237990 (Size standard $45M)? (Yes/No). If No, what estimated percentage do you think can be subcontracted out to small business? The U.S. Government is not obligated to pay for any information, documentation, demonstrations, or data provided, nor will it reimburse any costs incurred by your organization in preparing responses, traveling to, or participating in this Industry Day and physical equipment inspection. All costs associated with attending this event and participating in this information exchange are solely at the responding party�s expense. The affected parts are wholly owned by FMS customer countries, are not covered by a Cooperative Logistics Supply Support Arrangement (CLSSA), these same assets will be delivered to the customer country for their sole use. The IUID definition at DFARS 211.274-1 says IUID "is a system of marking, valuing and tracking items delivered to DoD." These spares are non-CLSSA FMS assets and will never be delivered to DoD. title: B-52 Data Interface Unit/Data Transfer Receptacle (DTR) - Buy and Repair F3I DTR
description: B-52 Data Interface Unit/Data Transfer Receptacle (DTR) The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources with the expertise, capabilities, experience, facilities, and technical capacity necessary to manufacture/provide and repair the B-52 Data Interface Unit/Data Transfer Receptacle (DTR). The National Stock Number (NSN) and Part Number (PN) are as follows: LRU: NSN 7025-01-738-4504AY, P/N P210015K0001-1, INTERFACE UNIT, DATA This Request for Information (RFI) supports a buy and repair requirement for the new Form, Fit, Function, and Interface (F3I) DTR. Kihomac, Inc. is currently manufacturing the F3I DTR under contract SPRWA1-21-D-0015. The Government owns, or will provide under appropriate controls, the manufacturing and technical data necessary to support competitive production and repair of this item. The Government intends to compete this requirement on the open market to obtain new production units and repair services. The legacy B-52 DTR is repaired by Symetrics Industries (CAGE 22830) under contracts FA8539-20-D-0013 and FA8539-25-D-0004. This market research effort pertains to the F3I DTR identified above, currently being manufactured by Kihomac, Inc. under contract SPRWA1-21-D-0015, and is intended to identify sources capable of supporting competitive manufacture and repair using Government-owned technical data. The DTR is a Line Replaceable Unit (LRU) on the B-52 aircraft, with two DTRs installed per aircraft. The DTR transfers Offensive Avionics System (OAS) information to and from storage on the Data Transfer Cartridge (DTC) across its interface with the Fibre Channel or MIL-STD-1553A data bus system. Additionally, the DTR provides status over the MIL-STD-1553A and Fibre Channel buses indicating that the DTC is successfully installed. The required scope shall include, as applicable, manufacture and delivery of new production DTR units; hardware repair and return of unserviceable DTR units; obsolete parts resolution; engineering support to investigate Deficiency Reports (DRs); Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages (DMSMS) support; development, maintenance, and execution of required inspection, test, and acceptance procedures; and configuration management support to ensure newly manufactured and repaired units conform to the applicable Government-furnished technical data package. All newly manufactured and repaired units must meet applicable form, fit, function, and interface requirements. The contractor shall furnish all necessary material, support equipment, tools, test equipment, facilities, and services required to perform the work. The contractor is responsible for acquiring, maintaining, and calibrating all support equipment required at its primary or subcontractor facilities. Contractor-furnished material or replacement parts must equal or exceed the quality, tolerances, and specifications identified in the applicable technical data package. INSTRUCTIONS: 1. The document(s) below contain a description of the NSN listed for buy and repair requirements and a Contractor Capability Survey. The Survey allows Contractors to provide their company�s capability. 2. If, after reviewing these documents, you wish to participate in this market research, you should provide documentation demonstrating your company's capability to meet these buy and repair requirements. Failure to provide adequate documentation may prevent the government from properly assessing your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please explain how you would overcome this deficiency to fulfill the requirement (e.g., through teaming or subcontracting). a. Identify any specific areas of work that your organization believes should be set aside exclusively for Small Business. 3. Questions regarding this market survey should be addressed to Tyler Martens, Program Manager, 478-955-5165 or via email at tyler.martens.2@us.af.mil. title: BAFS Construction Material and Delivery
description: This Request for Quotation (RFQ) is issued by the Air Force Installation Contracting Center (AFICC), 766th Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (766 ESS). This RFQ is a solicitation for a firm-fixed-price commercial supply purchase order. The Government intends to make an award based on quotations received in response to this RFQ. SOLICITATION INFORMATION: This acquisition is being conducted on a full and open competition basis. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 212319, Other Crushed and Broken Stone Mining and Quarrying, with a corresponding small-business size standard of 550 employees. No socioeconomic set-aside applies. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT: The Contractor shall furnish and deliver approximately 1,000 short tons of 1.5-inch (37.5 mm nominal maximum) dense-graded basalt aggregate base course to the Tinker Bridge Bypass Corridor, Bellows Air Force Station (BAFS), Waimanalo, Hawaii. This is a commercial supply requirement with incidental delivery. Government personnel will perform spreading, shaping, moisture conditioning, and compaction. The aggregate shall comply with ASTM D2940/D2940M and Hawaii Department of Transportation (HDOT) Highways Division Standard Specifications, Section 703.06. The Contractor shall furnish the material; perform quarry weighing and hauling; tailgate dump or stockpile at Government-designated locations; provide certified automated scale tickets for each load; and provide a current certified quarry quality-control sieve analysis. Quoters may be quarry producers, suppliers, or distributors, provided they furnish compliant material from a qualified quarry and meet all delivery requirements. description: Amendment 2: The purpose of this amendment is to change the response date from 16 November 2026 to 23 November 2026. Amendment 1: The purpose of this amendment is to change the response date from 16 November 2027 to 16 November 2026. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION MULTI-SOURCE PNT UE 1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes (market research). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation (Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotations (RFQ)) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Furthermore, the Government is not, at this time, seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Due to the operational sensitivity of the Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) missions, any future acquisition resulting from this market research will require strict adherence to Department of War (DoW) and Department of Defense (DoD) security, cybersecurity, and supply chain integrity standards. Consequently, while direct responses to this RFI must remain entirely unclassified (reach out to the government contacts below for information on classified submissions), respondents are required to demonstrate their organizational posture regarding facility clearances, information safeguarding, and National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) supply chain compliance. For the purposes of this market research, the anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for manufacturing global positioning systems (GPS) and related equipment is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing) with a Small Business Size Standard of $44.0 Million, and the primary Product Service Code (PSC) for Global Positioning Systems (GPS) hardware is 5825 (Radio Navigation Equipment, Except Airborne). For specialized, airborne GPS or radar navigation, the code is typically 5826. System-level R&D and engineering services for GPS are usually categorized under codes like R425 (Engineering Services) or AC13 (R&D�Defense System: Electronics). 2.0 BACKGROUND With advances in autonomous systems and guided munitions, the force that can best synchronize its activities at a single point in time and space wields a potent strategic advantage. In the future operating environment, therefore, the Joint Force will increasingly depend on resilient, reliable, and precise position, navigation, and timing (PNT) data to execute combat operations. As such, the Space Force is required to deliver global continuous coverage with stringent civil and military position and timing requirements to assure safety and mission success. This includes at least 88% of the constellation being operationally available more than 98% of the time. Likewise, a thinking adversary will make focused and deliberate efforts to deny access to this capability, leveraging a growing suite of threats including electromagnetic weapons, cyberspace attacks, and kinetic weapons. The challenge today is that, while satellite navigation (SATNAV) through the Global Positioning System (GPS) is foundational to U.S. military operations, critical infrastructure, and global commerce, the current architecture must adapt to evolving jamming and spoofing threats. Additionally, the space and ground segments must be modernized and hardened against physical attack. To build readiness for the future operating environment, therefore, the Space Force will pursue a comprehensive navigation warfare (NAVWAR) strategy that emphasizes resilience, technology modernization, modularity, adaptability, and flexibility. Specifically, it will adopt an open hybrid approach to SATNAV architecture that weighs inputs from diverse sources according to user need, generating a more dependable capability that can withstand adversary action while enabling faster upgrade cycles to enable PNT capabilities. The NAVWAR Objective Force pursues the development and deployment of several key capabilities to advance the SATNAV architecture. One of those elements is User Segment. To make best use of diversified PNT sources, the Space Force will enable a transition to a Multi-Source PNT user equipment (UE) reference architecture that incorporates Modular Open System Architectures (MOSA) and an onboard fusion engine to integrate all available data at the user level. The key enabler of the NAVWAR Objective Force is continued Joint Force investment in Multi-Source PNT UE that utilizes both traditional and new PNT sources. This equipment is foundational to a user�s ability to devise and execute a NAVWAR PACE (i.e., Primary / Alternate / Contingency / Emergency) Plan in degraded or denied environments. While legacy signals are expected to remain supported for civil and public functions, they are increasingly less effective in the contested environment. The military-specific M-Code is available today, while the PNT modernization signals are projected to be available by 2035. 3.0 OBJECTIVE, DESIRED CAPABILITIES AND CHARACTERISTICS This Request for Information (RFI) is focused on obtaining access to analytical information on industrial capabilities in Multi-Source PNT UE the NAVWAR Objective Force. Interests include the following: Multi-Source PNT UE for Terrestrial Users on various military platforms Disadvantaged user High value military assets MOSA Signals supported (M-code, CA, commercial), etc Space Service Volume Multi-Source PNT UE (various orbits) Small satellite users Large satellite users MOSA Signals supported (M-code, CA, commercial), etc Interest is in technical details that can be incorporated into technical analysis to support Space Warfighting Analysis Center, Technology and Emerging Concept Assessments performed during Force Designs. This RFI is being executed in cooperation with the Space Warfighting Analysis Center (SWAC). 4.0 SECURITY, CYBERSECURITY AND SUPPLY CHAIN REQUIREMENTS The secure nature of this requirement dictates adherence to stringent Department of War (DoW) / Department of Defense (DoD) security protocols. While direct responses to this RFI must remain unclassified, respondents shall address their current capabilities and compliance regarding the following security domains: a. Facility and Personnel Security Clearances Given the operational nature of Multi-Source PNT UE and the potential for integration with multiple military architectures, e?orts will likely require access to classified information and systems. Respondents must state their current Facility Clearance Level (FCL) (e.g., None, Secret, Top Secret) and classified safeguarding capabilities. Respondents should confirm their capacity to provide appropriately cleared personnel (Personnel Security Clearances - PCL) and facility infrastructure to support secure development, testing, and operations. Please indicate your facility's current capability and experience in handling, storing, and integrating Communications Security (COMSEC) and Transmission Security (TRANSEC) materials. b. Cybersecurity and Information Safeguarding (CUI/CDI) The protection of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and Covered Defense Information (CDI) is critical to this effort. In accordance with DFARS 252.204-7012, 7019, and 7020, respondents must describe their current capability to safeguard CUI/CDI. description: Amendment 0004 is hereby posted. ________________________________________________________________________ Amendment 0003 is hereby posted. ________________________________________________________________________ Amendment 0002 is hereby posted. ________________________________________________________________________ Amendment 0001 is hereby posted. ________________________________________________________________________ The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS), is seeking a qualified contractor for construction services for the Gate 7 Parking Garage at the St. Elizabeths West Campus in Southeast Washington, DC. GSA anticipates awarding a single Firm-Fixed-Price construction contract for the new construction of the Gate 7 Parking Garage and associated site, utility, security, stormwater, landscape, and infrastructure improvements. The project will support the operational needs of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) at the St. Elizabeths West Campus. This acquisition is for construction services only. The project design is being completed separately by GSA�s Architect of Record, ZGF. The construction solicitation is based on Issued for Construction drawings, specifications, and related contract documents. The work to be performed under the terms of this contract includes, but is not limited to, furnishing all management, supervision, subcontractors, labor, materials, supplies, tools, equipment, coordination, quality control, testing, inspections, commissioning support, and closeout documentation necessary to construct the Gate 7 Parking Garage in accordance with the contract documents. The project includes construction of a new multi-level parking garage with associated surface parking, access and screening infrastructure, and related campus improvements. The anticipated scope includes, but is not limited to: Site development, clearing, grading, excavation, and civil infrastructure improvements Utility relocations, extensions, tie-ins, and connections Substructure construction, including foundations, slab-on-grade, excavation support, waterproofing, and retaining walls Parking garage structure, including structural framing, parking decks, ramps, stairs, elevators, roof assemblies, and related structural components Mechanically ventilated parking garage systems, including ventilation equipment, shafts, ductwork, louvers or openings, controls, electrical power, life-safety interfaces, testing, balancing, and commissioning support Exterior fa�ade and building envelope construction, including a classical architectural brick fa�ade with openings Exterior doors, windows, louvers, waterproofing, sealants, flashings, and related envelope components Mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, fire alarm, emergency communications, lighting, controls, IT, telecommunications, electronic security, access control, CCTV, parking guidance, and related systems Physical security elements, including vehicle barriers, bollards, gates, credentialing areas, and screening-related infrastructure Roadway, shuttle, pedestrian circulation, hardscape, landscape, site lighting, signage, and related site improvements Stormwater management facilities, erosion and sediment control, and environmental protection measures Testing, inspections, commissioning support, training, warranties, as-built documentation, BIM/COBie deliverables where applicable, and project closeout The Gate 7 Parking Garage will be constructed within the active St. Elizabeths West Campus, a high-security federal campus and National Historic Landmark. The contractor will be required to coordinate construction activities with ongoing campus operations, security requirements, occupied facilities, existing utilities, shuttle operations, adjacent work, traffic and access impacts, and protection of historic and environmental resources. The contractor may also be required to coordinate with District of Columbia agencies or authorities, as applicable, for traffic control, haul routes, public space, utility, roadway, permit, or other construction-related requirements. All work shall conform to applicable GSA requirements, the 2026 PBS Core Building Standards, contract drawings and specifications, campus security requirements, applicable codes and standards, and project-specific requirements. The estimated cost range for construction is between $120,000,000.00 and $160,000,000.00. The contractor will be required to coordinate construction activities with ongoing campus operations, security requirements, occupied facilities, existing utilities, shuttle operations, adjacent work, traffic and access impacts, and protection of historic and environmental resources. The contractor may also be required to coordinate with District of Columbia agencies or authorities, as applicable, for traffic control, haul routes, public space, utility, roadway, permit, or other construction-related requirements. All work shall conform to applicable GSA requirements, the 2026 PBS Core Building Standards, contract drawings and specifications, campus security requirements, applicable codes and standards, and project-specific requirements. The estimated cost range for construction is between $120,000,000.00 and $160,000,000.00. The intended project delivery method is a Phased Acquisition procurement using a Two-Phase Construction Concept. title: Finland – Miscellaneous repair and maintenance services – Pesulakoneiden toimitukset ja asennukset sekä huoltotoiminnot / VAV
description: Tilaajan tavoitteena on hankkia joustava yhteistyökumppani Vantaalla sijaitsevien VAV-konsernin omistamien kiinteistöjen pesuloiden ja kuivaushuoneiden uusien koneiden toimituksiin, asennuksiin sekä niiden huoltotoimintoihin. Tarkemmin tiloihin ja laitekantaan voi tutustua oheisesta kohdeluettelosta. Tilastojen mukaan pesula- ja kuivaushuoneiden koneuusintoihin liittyviä toimeksiantoja esiintyisi tässä kiinteistökannassa noin 60 kpl / vuosi. Tilastojen mukaan pesula- ja kuivaushuoneiden konehuoltoihin liittyviä vikatarkastus-/korjauksia esiintyisi tässä kiinteistökannassa noin 360 kpl / vuosi, jonka lisäksi Tilaajalla on ennakoivaa vuosihuoltotoimintaa. Sopimus ei sisällä määräostovelvoitetta. Tilaaja ei sitoudu hankintailmoituksessa esitettyihin arvioihin hankintamääristä. Tilaaja pitää erityisen tärkeänä, että pesula- ja kuivaushuoneissa käytettävät koneet huolletaan systemaattisesti ("vuosihuollot"). Lisäksi arjessa esiintyvät muunlaiset vikakorjaukset tehdään ripeästi ja että koneet uusitaan elinkaariajattelu huomioiden kustannustehokkaasti. Uusien pesulakoneiden toimituksissa ja asennuksissa palveluun kuuluu mm.: • Pesula- ja kuivaushuoneiden laitekannan uusiminen Tilaajan kanssa erikseen sopien Pesulakoneiden huoltotoiminnassa palveluun kuuluu mm.: • Laitteiden ennakoiva vuosihuoltotoiminta • Kuivausrummun huoltotoimet vikaantumisissa • Pesukoneen poisto-/tuloputken huollot, virran antoon liittyvien vikojen selvittely ja ohjauspaneelien huolto-/ korjaustoimet • Mankelin erilaiset huolto-/korjaustoimet • Kuivaushuoneen puhaltimien virhetilanteiden hoitaminen Työtilauksiin voi sisältyä myös tarvikehankintoja ja muita työn suorittamiseen liittyviä palveluhankintoja. Tavoitteiden saavuttamisen edellytykset on kerrottu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön ESPD-lomakkeella, hankinnan kohteen kriteerit -osiossa sekä hankintailmoituksen liitteissä. Hankintapäätöksen tekoperusteena on kokonaistaloudellinen edullisuus pisteytyksen mukaisesti, jossa maksimipisteet ovat 1000 pistettä. Tarjoajan on annettava tarjous kaikista tarjouslomakkeen töistä. Mikäli Tarjoaja ei ole tarjonnut kaikkia tarjouslomakkeeseen eriteltyjä töitä, tulkitaan tarjous puutteelliseksi. Puutteellinen tarjous hylätään. Tarjoajan kannalta huomioitavaa on myös se, että tarjottujen töiden ja hintojen tulee sisältää kaikki tässä tarjouspyynnössä, hankintasopimusluonnoksessa ja palvelukuvauksessa määritellyt kriteerit. Palvelu toteutetaan tarjouspyynnön, palvelukuvauksen ja laatuvaatimusten mukaisesti. Tarjoajan antama tarjous on sitova. Hankintasopimus syntyy vasta kirjallisen sopimuksen allekirjoittamisella, selonottoneuvottelujen jälkeen. EU-kynnysarvon ylittävässä hankinnassa sopimus voidaan tehdä aikaisintaan 14 vuorokauden kuluttua siitä, kun Tarjoaja on saanut tai hänen katsotaan saaneen päätöksen perusteluineen tiedoksi. Tarjoaja ei saa esittää esimerkiksi omissa tarjousasiakirjoissaan ehtoja, jotka vaikuttaisivat hankintasopimuksen sisältöön. Sopimuskauden tavoitealkamisajankohta on 1.4.2027 ja sopimus on voimassa toistaiseksi.

title: N--SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment by the Government. Responses will be used for market research purposes to determine the availability of qualified sources and to support acquisition planning. No reimbursement will be provided for responding to this notice. The Government is not seeking proposals at this time. This notice does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. Any future solicitation will be posted separately on SAM.gov, and interested parties are responsible for monitoring that site. 1. Purpose: The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) is conducting market research to identify qualified small business concerns, including Small Business, Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), HUBZone Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB), Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEE), and 8(a) firms, capable of providing all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, transportation, crane services, and other resources necessary to furnish and install two marine radar systems (brand name or equal to Furuno) aboard the Research Vessel (R/V) KIYI. The requirement includes the procurement of two radar systems and all associated components, removal of existing radar equipment and cabling, installation of the new radar systems, system integration, testing, commissioning, and turnover or disposal of removed equipment as directed by the Government. The R/V KIYI is located at its home port in Ashland, Wisconsin, where all work will be performed. 2. Background: The R/V KIYI currently utilizes two Furuno FAR 21X7 radar systems that are obsolete and no longer supported by the manufacturer. Following the failure of one radar and the unavailability of replacement parts, the USGS has determined that both radar systems must be replaced to ensure continued safe and reliable vessel operations. 3. Requirement: The contractor shall furnish and install two marine radar systems (brand name or equal to Furuno), including all associated components, removal of existing radar systems and cabling, installation, integration with existing vessel electronics, testing, commissioning, and crane services required for antenna removal and installation. The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, materials, tools, transportation, and equipment necessary to complete the requirement. 4. Period of Performance: Five (5) months from date of award. 5. NAICS and PSC: NAICS: 334511 - Search, Detection, Navigation, Guidance, Aeronautical, and Nautical System and Instrument Manufacturing Size Standard: 1,350 Employees PSC: N059 - Installation of Equipment, Electrical and Electronic Equipment Components 6. SAM Registration: All interested firms must be registered in SAM.gov to be eligible for a future award. Registration information is available at https://www.sam.gov. 7. Requested Information: Interested firms shall submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide and install marine radar systems meeting the requirements described herein. At a minimum, responses shall include: 1. Company name, UEI, CAGE Code, and business size/socioeconomic status. 2. A description of the firm's experience performing similar marine radar installation and integration projects within the last five years. 3. Examples of at least three relevant projects, including customer, contract value, period of performance, and a brief description of the work performed. 4. A description of the firm's technical capabilities, personnel qualifications, and equipment necessary to perform the required work. 5. Identification of any authorized relationships with Furuno or equivalent marine radar manufacturers. 6. Identification of whether the firm is the manufacturer, authorized reseller, integrator, installer, or other provider of the proposed equipment. 7. Identification of any anticipated subcontracting and the portion of work to be subcontracted. 8. Confirmation of the firm's ability to perform the work in Ashland, Wisconsin. 9. Identification of any concerns with the proposed NAICS code, PSC, or size standard. 10. If the requirement were set aside for small business, would your firm be capable of performing as the prime contractor? Ensure your firm's UEI, CAGE Code, and socioeconomic representations are current in SAM.gov. Capability statements should not exceed five (5) pages. 8. Submission Instructions: Interested firms shall submit a capabilities package addressing all elements identified above to beth_wilson@ios.doi.gov no later than close of business on November 23, 2026. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice are not adequate responses to any future solicitation. If a solicitation is released, it will be announced separately on SAM.gov. The Government will not review capability statements for the purpose of pre-qualifying vendors for any future solicitation.

Our mission supports the deepening and the maintenance dredging of the Delaware River and Wilmington Harbor. Heavy Equipment is utilized to construct dikes, ditching for drying and other dirt work. Our equipment is currently composed of D6 Dozers, Excavators (tracks and pontoons), dump trucks (articulated). Without equipment to provide the necessary dirt work in these disposals� areas, dredging assignments in the Delaware Harbor could not be accomplished. title: PACA Special Audits RFQ
description: General The Air Force Services Center (AFSVC), headquartered at Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland, Texas, delivers Services programs and activities to build and sustain ready and resilient Airmen, Guardians, and families. Air Force Services Center supports bases, major commands (MAJCOMs), and the Air Staff by providing technical expertise, launching new initiatives, developing programs and operational procedures, and managing central support functions. Air Force Services Center ensures the successful operation of essential food services, fitness and sports centers, childcare and youth programs, lodging accommodations, and recreational opportunities for military members and their families worldwide. The Center�s responsibilities include preparing responses to high-level inquiries, providing technical assistance to the field, and developing new programs supporting installation activities. The Financial Management Directorate (VF) centrally manages and administers the Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) Public Accountant Contract Audit (PACA) Program, which supports a worldwide mission providing independent oversight of internal controls, cash management, asset protection, and financial management across the enterprise. Background Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations provide support services and activities for military personnel, families, and authorized patrons. Proper management and accountability of Nonappropriated Fund resources are critical to ensuring continued service delivery, operational readiness, and the protection of government interests. Regular independent audits are required to evaluate the financial condition, control environments, and operational efficiencies of Nonappropriated Fund operations. The Air Force Services Center Financial Management, Strategic Policy & Financial Operations Branch (AFSVC/VFSF) exercises central program oversight to ensure compliance with annual statutory audit requirements under Department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 7600.06, Audit of Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities and Related Activities, ensuring adequate audit coverage is provided across the enterprise for Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) Services activities. The term "Activities" refers to operational and revenue-generating entities within the Air Force structure. Audit engagements under this Special Audits contract specifically include financial statement audits and performance audits covering: � Accounting practices and transactional compliance; � Internal control environments and segregation of duties; � Cash management, vault operations, and electronic banking; � Fixed asset accountability, tracking, and depreciation; � Inventory valuation, spoilage controls, and physical counts; � Food and beverage operations and food service portfolios; � Centralized shared service center processing; � Venture gaming and electronic slot machine operations; � Supplemental mission dining operations; and � Agreed-upon procedures and special interest compliance reviews. Specific Focus Areas for the PACA Special Audits Program: � A. Shared Service Center (SSC): Conduct performance audits of the Shared Service Center (SSC) at the Air Force Services Center (AFSVC) located in San Antonio, TX. The primary objective of the performance audit is to address economy, efficiency, and operational effectiveness. The scope includes core accounting transaction workflows, inter-entity cost allocation methodologies, compliance with Service Level Agreements (SLAs), operational metrics, and the adequacy of financial management technology system controls. Further details will be outlined in specific delivery order project assignments. � B. Department of the Air Force (DAF) Venture Gaming Program: The DAF Venture Gaming Program operates electronic gaming and slot machine activities at authorized overseas military installations. The program serves as an important nonappropriated revenue generator utilized directly to support and enhance Morale, Welfare, and Recreation (MWR) programs across all Air Force installations. Authorized by DoDI 1015.10 and centrally managed by AFSVC in San Antonio, TX, slot machine operations present unique risks due to regulatory complexities, high cash volumes, and potential for manipulation. Scope includes electronic gaming data systems, meter reconciliations, cash drop and count controls, payout authorizations, jackpot disbursements, internal control safeguards against manipulation or theft, and compliance with federal tax reporting requirements (including IRS Form W-2G processing). � C. Air Force Cadet Dining Fund: The Cadet Dining Fund is a Supplemental Mission Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) operated by the 10th Force Support Squadron (10th FSS) located at the United States Air Force Academy (USAFA), Colorado. Supplemental Mission NAFIs receive nonappropriated funds generated from installation mission programs (training, food service, education, security). While congressionally appropriated funds (APF) cover civilian management, custodial services, and facility upkeep, nonappropriated funds are utilized strictly for food purchases and the operational maintenance of cadet meal operations. The fund provides daily dining support for over 4,400 cadets. The Contractor shall perform comprehensive financial statement and operational compliance audits examining food supply procurement, inventory receiving and storage controls, cost-per-meal accounting, meal card verifications, and financial statement accuracy in accordance with USAFAI 34-104 and applicable NAF regulations. � D. Commander�s Special Interest Audits: To address immediate, unplanned operational needs, the Government requires the capacity to execute ad hoc, targeted investigations known as Commander�s Special Interest Audits. These audits may be requested at any given time by Installation Commanders, the AFSVC Commander, or higher headquarters to address immediate operational concerns, suspected material control failures, or strategic risk areas. These ad hoc engagements may encompass any Air Force Installation, NAF Activity, or fund within the scope of this contract, and will be ordered and executed as individual, consolidated performance audit task orders in accordance with the established deliverables and pricing schedules. Scope Air Force Services Center requires the audit services of licensed Certified Public Accountants (CPAs) or CPA firms to perform financial statement audits of Air Force Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) financial statements and performance audits of Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) Services activities, with particular emphasis on high-risk areas identified through preliminary risk assessments and annual selection matrices.

title: Alternative Protein Technologies for Military Field Feeding
description: SYNOPSIS: This Sources Sought Announcement is to assist the US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command - Soldier Center (DEVCOM-SC) to identify potential sources to provide innovative product development research and/or consumer research and/or demonstration food samples in the area of alternative proteins. Responses are limited to Massachusetts based offerors as determined by CAGE code. The Government requests responders submit a Broad Agency Announcement BAA preproposal as outlined in DEVCOM-SC BAA W911QY-25-R-0023 located at: https://sam.gov/opp/a5ec94e2baee40df9951f864a8665e71/view Please refer to Section VI - Scientific and Technical Areas of Interest, A. Combat Ration Research and Development. Submit the BAA preproposal to: michael.s.wiederoder.civ@army.mil, richard.j.green.civ@army.mil and jean.m.trumpis.civ@army.mil by 23 November 2026, 5:00 PM EST. OBJECTIVE: DEVCOM-SC seeks product development, consumer research, and food sample demonstrations of current and emerging novel alternative protein technologies that could be integrated into military rations. BACKGROUND: The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Soldier Center (DEVCOM-SC), Combat Feeding Division (CFD), is seeking information from industry and academia on capabilities related to alternative proteins. The U.S. Army is exploring how the emerging alternative-protein sector can help meet several objectives, including enhancing food supply chain resilience, enabling biomanufacturing of foodstuffs in combat-forward environments, and providing tailored, high-quality nutrition to the Warfighter. DEVCOM-SC CFD has unique expertise in the development and assessment of shelf-stable ration components, as well as food safety and palatability for the Joint Warfighter. We are looking to partner with the commercial and academic sectors to advance technology development in this area. AREAS OF INTEREST: DEVCOM-SC is seeking information from offerors that can provide capabilities in one or more of the following areas. Work proposed should be to advance technology between TRL 4 and 6. Please note, for the purposes of this Sources Sought, we are specifically excluding solutions related to cell-cultured, lab-grown meat or insect protein. Innovative technologies for alternative protein development to reduce Soldier load: Seeking advanced technologies and processes involved in fermentation, precision fermentation, or other novel biomanufacturing methods, that enhance the production of alternative proteins where additional funding in specific components of the research would significantly accelerate advancements in technology between TRL 4 and 6, enabling faster transition to operational use. These technologies should focus on creating lightweight and nutrient-dense ration solutions to reduce logistical burdens and physical load on warfighters while maintaining or enhancing nutritional value and operational performance. Innovative Product Development: The development of innovative meat-alternative products specifically designed for inclusion in military rations, meeting stringent requirements for nutrition, shelf stability, and palatability. Consumer Research and Acceptability: The ability to conduct comprehensive consumer research (e.g., focus groups, sensory panels, field testing) to enhance the acceptability and consumption of alternative proteins within a military population. Food Sample Demonstration: An optional addition to the effort would be to provide 100 food samples of a potential product that has Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) status with an FDA no-questions letter to demonstrate the maturation of an alternative protein manufacturing technology. These samples would be provided to the Government for sensory acceptability and other performance characteristics and will be consumed by our test panel of experts. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Interested parties (companies or academic institutions) are requested to submit a proposal that details their capabilities in one or more of the areas listed in Section 3.0. Submissions should include: A detailed description of your technical approach. Relevant past performance or corporate experience. A rough order of magnitude (ROM) cost estimate for the proposed work or samples. This information will be used for market research and planning purposes. Responses to this Sources Sought are not binding proposals, but they will help shape future solicitation requirements. Offerors are welcome to send samples at their own cost for evaluation. DEVCOM SC will not return any items, nor is DEVCOM SC obligated to share any data from evaluation. Sending samples is not required for consideration for funding. Samples must be GRAS with an FDA no-questions letter. Please coordinate by e-mail (richard.j.green.civ@army.mil) before sending samples. Address information will be provided at that time. SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. This Sources Sought Announcement is issued solely for information and planning purposes and to identify interested sources. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. No contract will be awarded from this announcement. This Sources Sought does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. It is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. Further, unsolicited proposals will not be accepted. Funding is not available at this time. The United States Army has not made a commitment to procure any of the items/services discussed, and release of this Sources Sought Announcement should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. Response to this Sources Sought Announcement is voluntary and no reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this and any follow-on information requests. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this Sources Sought Announcement does not preclude participation in any future RFP if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the SAM.gov website. It is the responsibility of the potential responders to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this subject. RESPONSES: Interested parties may identify their interest and capability by sending BAA preproposals regarding this requirement to DEVCOM-SC via e-mail ONLY to michael.s.wiederoder.civ@army.mil, richard.j.green.civ@army.mil and jean.m.trumpis.civ@army.mil by 23 November 2026, 5:00 PM EST. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this Notice. All costs associated with responding to this Notice will be solely at the expense of the interested party. Submissions should include: Whether you are proposing product development and/or consumer research and/or sample demonstration. A detailed description of your technical approach. Relevant past performance or corporate experience. A rough order of magnitude (ROM) cost estimate for the proposed work or samples. Please provide business size (indicate your socioeconomic status), applicable NAICS code, and CAGE code. QUESTIONS: Any questions for clarification may be emailed to michael.s.wiederoder.civ@army.mil, richard.j.green.civ@army.mil and jean.m.trumpis.civ@army.mil no later than 18 November 2026, 5:00 PM EST. Verbal questions will NOT be accepted. Questions shall NOT contain proprietary or classified information. An unattributed list of questions and answers will be published at the same web location of this Sources Sought Announcement.

The Penetrator Weapons Branch (AFLCMC/EBDP), Attack Division (AFLCMC/EBD), Armament Directorate (AFLCMC/EB), Eglin AFB, FL, plans to award a firm-fixed price/Cost-type multiple award Indefinite-Delivery Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract for the development through production of the NGP program. The work required is in support of the NGP program at Eglin AFB and includes work to support all aspects of research & development, production, testing, and delivery of the NGP weapon system. No TDPs will be released for this presolicitation and draft solicitation. North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 332993 with a size standard of 1,500 employees. The Government anticipates awarding multiple contracts utilizing The Department of Defense Source Selection Procedures. Anticipated date of official solicitation release is on or about mid December 2026. The Government will not provide a hard copy of the solicitation. Future information pertaining to this requirement will be posted on the System for Award Management (SAM) website (SAM.gov). Interested parties should monitor the SAM website for changes. Foreign participation IS NOT authorized as a prime contractor or as a subcontractor. Draft Solicitation Documents: Many of the draft solicitation documents referenced within are Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), Distribution F. This information will only be provided to those contractors that are registered and active in the Joint Certification Program (JCP) through the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA). To receive these draft solicitation documents, interested parties must officially request these documents in writing, via e-mail, with a valid DD Form 2345 to Mandi Johnson at mandi.johnson.4@us.af.mil and Christy Cross at christy.cross.2@us.af.mil. The draft solicitation documents will only be sent to the data custodian listed within the Joint Certification Program (JCP) system. The draft solicitation documents will only be sent to interested vendors with a valid DD2345 via DoDSAFE. Interested parties to this solicitation are encouraged to request the draft solicitation documents to review and provide any comments or questions to Contracting Officer, Mandi Johnson at mandi.johnson.4@us.af.mil and the Contract Specialist, Christy Cross at christy.cross.2@us.af.mil by 4:00 P.M. CST on 23 November 2026. For clarification nothing other than questions and comments to the draft solicitation will be accepted at this time. This posting is not for interested parties to submit their proposals. The Government intends to review all comments/questions and incorporate the feedback that proves beneficial to improve clarity of the upcoming solicitation. **NOTE: It is highly advised that if you wish to participate in this effort that your DD Form 2345 be updated and filed to reflect current personnel, etc..**

title: PACA Special Audits RFQ
description: General The Air Force Services Center (AFSVC), headquartered at Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland, Texas, delivers Services programs and activities to build and sustain ready and resilient Airmen, Guardians, and families. Air Force Services Center supports bases, major commands (MAJCOMs), and the Air Staff by providing technical expertise, launching new initiatives, developing programs and operational procedures, and managing central support functions. Air Force Services Center ensures the successful operation of essential food services, fitness and sports centers, childcare and youth programs, lodging accommodations, and recreational opportunities for military members and their families worldwide. The Center�s responsibilities include preparing responses to high-level inquiries, providing technical assistance to the field, and developing new programs supporting installation activities. The Financial Management Directorate (VF) centrally manages and administers the Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) Public Accountant Contract Audit (PACA) Program, which supports a worldwide mission providing independent oversight of internal controls, cash management, asset protection, and financial management across the enterprise. Background Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations provide support services and activities for military personnel, families, and authorized patrons. Proper management and accountability of Nonappropriated Fund resources are critical to ensuring continued service delivery, operational readiness, and the protection of government interests. Regular independent audits are required to evaluate the financial condition, control environments, and operational efficiencies of Nonappropriated Fund operations. The Air Force Services Center Financial Management, Strategic Policy & Financial Operations Branch (AFSVC/VFSF) exercises central program oversight to ensure compliance with annual statutory audit requirements under Department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 7600.06, Audit of Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities and Related Activities, ensuring adequate audit coverage is provided across the enterprise for Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) Services activities. The term "Activities" refers to operational and revenue-generating entities within the Air Force structure. Audit engagements under this Special Audits contract specifically include financial statement audits and performance audits covering: � Accounting practices and transactional compliance; � Internal control environments and segregation of duties; � Cash management, vault operations, and electronic banking; � Fixed asset accountability, tracking, and depreciation; � Inventory valuation, spoilage controls, and physical counts; � Food and beverage operations and food service portfolios; � Centralized shared service center processing; � Venture gaming and electronic slot machine operations; � Supplemental mission dining operations; and � Agreed-upon procedures and special interest compliance reviews. Specific Focus Areas for the PACA Special Audits Program: � A. Shared Service Center (SSC): Conduct performance audits of the Shared Service Center (SSC) at the Air Force Services Center (AFSVC) located in San Antonio, TX. The primary objective of the performance audit is to address economy, efficiency, and operational effectiveness. The scope includes core accounting transaction workflows, inter-entity cost allocation methodologies, compliance with Service Level Agreements (SLAs), operational metrics, and the adequacy of financial management technology system controls. Further details will be outlined in specific delivery order project assignments. � B. Department of the Air Force (DAF) Venture Gaming Program: The DAF Venture Gaming Program operates electronic gaming and slot machine activities at authorized overseas military installations. The program serves as an important nonappropriated revenue generator utilized directly to support and enhance Morale, Welfare, and Recreation (MWR) programs across all Air Force installations. Authorized by DoDI 1015.10 and centrally managed by AFSVC in San Antonio, TX, slot machine operations present unique risks due to regulatory complexities, high cash volumes, and potential for manipulation. Scope includes electronic gaming data systems, meter reconciliations, cash drop and count controls, payout authorizations, jackpot disbursements, internal control safeguards against manipulation or theft, and compliance with federal tax reporting requirements (including IRS Form W-2G processing). � C. Air Force Cadet Dining Fund: The Cadet Dining Fund is a Supplemental Mission Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) operated by the 10th Force Support Squadron (10th FSS) located at the United States Air Force Academy (USAFA), Colorado. Supplemental Mission NAFIs receive nonappropriated funds generated from installation mission programs (training, food service, education, security). While congressionally appropriated funds (APF) cover civilian management, custodial services, and facility upkeep, nonappropriated funds are utilized strictly for food purchases and the operational maintenance of cadet meal operations. The fund provides daily dining support for over 4,400 cadets. The Contractor shall perform comprehensive financial statement and operational compliance audits examining food supply procurement, inventory receiving and storage controls, cost-per-meal accounting, meal card verifications, and financial statement accuracy in accordance with USAFAI 34-104 and applicable NAF regulations. � D. Commander�s Special Interest Audits: To address immediate, unplanned operational needs, the Government requires the capacity to execute ad hoc, targeted investigations known as Commander�s Special Interest Audits. These audits may be requested at any given time by Installation Commanders, the AFSVC Commander, or higher headquarters to address immediate operational concerns, suspected material control failures, or strategic risk areas. These ad hoc engagements may encompass any Air Force Installation, NAF Activity, or fund within the scope of this contract, and will be ordered and executed as individual, consolidated performance audit task orders in accordance with the established deliverables and pricing schedules. Scope Air Force Services Center requires the audit services of licensed Certified Public Accountants (CPAs) or CPA firms to perform financial statement audits of Air Force Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) financial statements and performance audits of Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) Services activities, with particular emphasis on high-risk areas identified through preliminary risk assessments and annual selection matrices.
